clauses.statement: Every conformance violation carries a stable id derived deterministically from the element's own semantic values (kind plus involved file paths / module pair / normalized cycle member sequence), never from array position or group ordinal; scanning the same commit twice yields identical id sets and identical per-dimension counts.
clauses.rationale: Violation counts fluctuate per HEAD (measured 91/86/85/84/76), so base/head deltas are only trustworthy if violation identity survives unrelated changes; ordinal-based identity is a known trap that breaks under insertion.

clauses.statement: Given a base ref and a head ref, vibepro architecture conformance --base <ref> [--head <ref>] classifies every violation id into new / resolved / unchanged and reports a multi-dimensional summary that separates new-by-severity, resolved, existing, orphan files, budget violations, dependency cycles, and inconclusive — never a single flat violation_count as the distance signal.
clauses.rationale: Resolving two minor violations while adding one severe inverted dependency must not read as an improvement; dimensions must not be conflated.

clauses.statement: A scanner exception, a scan scope with zero source files, or a missing/unparseable target model degrades the conformance result to status inconclusive with a reason — never to a successful result with violation_count 0 — and a delta with an inconclusive side is itself inconclusive.
clauses.rationale: The architecture check crashed on a dirty real environment; had the count been read as zero, the failure would have presented as a clean repository. Measurement failure must be distinguishable from conformance.

clauses.rationale: The sensor must run on every PR without enforcement side effects: blocking belongs to the later ratchet-gate story, and an unpopulated conformance_summary is exactly the blindfolded-judgment failure this story removes.
